steps.say: Most kidney stones are calcium oxalate, and seven to eight in ten stones are counted in this chemistry. They are started on Randall plaques seated deep in the papilla, where calcium phosphate is deposited in the interstitium. Urine oxalate is layered over the plaque once it is exposed. Foods like spinach and nuts are reviewed, along with excess vitamin C intake. Low urine volume is corrected day and night, because concentrated urine grows every salt.
steps.tx: **Calcium oxalate** (commonest stone salt) forms **70% to 80%** (seven to eight in ten) of urinary calculi, starting on **Randall plaques** (calcium phosphate patches) in the renal papillary interstitium. Plaque erodes through the urothelium and gathers oxalate layers from concentrated urine. Keep urine dilute through the day and night, because volume is the cheapest prevention. Assess diet for spinach, nuts, and excess vitamin C.

vis.alt: Randall plaque in the renal papilla seeding a calcium oxalate stone.
vis.caption: Randall plaque: interstitial calcium phosphate seeds most calcium oxalate stones. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Uric acid stones are grown in persistently acid urine, and a pH below five point five day after day is the driver. Gout with obesity and insulin resistance is clustered here and raises the risk. The stones stay radiolucent on plain films, so a normal KUB is read as never excluding them. Every chemistry is displayed by non contrast CT regardless of density. The urine is alkalinized to dissolve small stones.
steps.tx: **Uric acid** (gout related stone) calculi form in persistently **acidic urine** (acid urine **below pH 5.5**), so gout, obesity, and insulin resistance raise risk. They are **radiolucent** (invisible on plain X-ray) on KUB films yet bright on **non-contrast CT** (plain stone CT), which sees every chemistry. Dissolve small stones with potassium citrate titrated to pH 6.5 to 7.0, because alkaline urine keeps urate soluble.

vis.alt: Uric acid metabolism and the effect of acid urine on stone formation.
vis.caption: Uric acid stones: acid urine below pH 5.5 grows radiolucent stones seen on CT. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Struvite stones are caused by chronic urinary infection, and urease splitting organisms drive the chemistry. Proteus mirabilis is blamed as the classic culprit, while Klebsiella pneumoniae behaves the same way. Ammonia is released and alkalinizes the urine above seven point two. Magnesium ammonium phosphate is precipitated fast into staghorn shapes. Infection is cleared and all fragments are removed, because residue is regrown quickly.
steps.tx: **Struvite** (infection stone) calculi mix **magnesium ammonium phosphate** (triple phosphate) with carbonate apatite and follow chronic infection with **urease** (urea splitting enzyme) organisms, classically **Proteus mirabilis** (swarming bacillus) and Klebsiella pneumoniae. Urease releases ammonia, pushes pH above 7.2, and precipitates stone rapidly into **staghorn** (antler shaped branched) casts. Clear infection and remove all fragments, because residue regrows quickly.

vis.alt: Staghorn struvite calculus filling the renal pelvis and calyces.
vis.caption: Staghorn calculus: infection stones branch across pelvis and calyces. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Cystine stones are inherited and keep returning through life. Autosomal recessive mutations are carried in SLC3A1 or SLC7A9 and break dibasic amino acid transport. Cystine with ornithine, lysine, and arginine is spilled together under the COLA memory tag. Stones are started in childhood or teens with bilateral disease. Every family is screened once a case is confirmed.
steps.tx: **Cystine** (inherited amino acid stone) calculi arise from autosomal recessive mutations in **SLC3A1** (chromosome 2 transporter) or **SLC7A9** (chromosome 19 transporter) that waste the **COLA** (cystine ornithine lysine arginine) dibasic amino acids into urine. Poorly soluble cystine precipitates from childhood with recurrent bilateral stones, so screen siblings early. Push fluids round the clock with potassium citrate, because dilution plus alkali is the base of prevention.

steps.say: The bedside cystine test is added to every stone workup for the young. Sodium nitroprusside reagent is mixed into urine and watched for colour. Cystine above seventy five mg per litre is turned magenta by the reagent. The purple change is accepted as pathognomonic for cystinuria. Every positive is confirmed by twenty four hour urine quantification.
steps.tx: **Brand test** (bedside cystine screen) adds **sodium nitroprusside** (alkaline reagent) to urine and turns **magenta** (deep purple) when cystine exceeds **75 mg/L** (seventy five milligrams per litre). The colour change is pathognomonic for cystinuria in a child or young adult with recurrent stones. Confirm every positive with 24 hour urine cystine quantification, because therapy and family screening rest on the numbers.

steps.say: Small distal ureteric stones are often passed alone without procedures. Passage is lifted by medical expulsive therapy in selected cases. Tamsulosin zero point four mg daily is prescribed as the standard choice. Stones of five to ten mm are helped most by relaxed distal muscle. Analgesia with a strainer is arranged for proof of passage. Fever with unremitting pain or a blocked solitary kidney is treated as an emergency.
steps.tx: **Medical expulsive therapy** (drugs aiding stone passage) with **tamsulosin 0.4 mg** (alpha-1 blocker) daily relaxes distal ureteric smooth muscle and lifts spontaneous passage of **5 mm to 10 mm** (five to ten millimetre) distal stones. Offer it with analgesia and a strainer for proof of passage. Stop and intervene for fever, unremitting pain, or obstruction of a solitary kidney, because infection behind a blockage is an emergency.

vis.alt: Distal ureteric stone causing hydroureter and acute renal colic.
vis.caption: Distal ureteric stone: 5 to 10 mm calculi may pass with tamsulosin. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Urine citrate is valued as a guard against calcium stones. Excretion below three hundred twenty mg a day is defined as hypocitraturia. Distal renal tubular acidosis is listed as a classic cause with chronic diarrhoea. High salt intake is added as a further lowering factor. Potassium citrate is dosed to hold urine pH between six point five and seven point zero.
steps.tx: **Hypocitraturia** (low urine citrate) below **320 mg/day** (three hundred twenty milligrams) removes a major brake on calcium crystallization, seen in distal renal tubular acidosis, chronic diarrhoea, and high salt diets. Replace it with **potassium citrate** (alkali salt) dosed to hold urine pH at **6.5 to 7.0** (six point five to seven). Recheck pH and citrate on therapy, because over alkalinization favours calcium phosphate stones.

steps.say: High urine calcium is blamed for most calcium recurrence. Excretion is lowered by thiazide diuretics acting on the tubule. Chlorthalidone twenty five mg daily is used as the first choice. Hydrochlorothiazide twenty five to fifty mg daily is kept as the alternative. Salt restriction is paired with normal dietary calcium on every prescription. Potassium with glucose and uric acid is monitored on follow up.
steps.tx: **Thiazide diuretics** (calcium lowering water pills), **chlorthalidone 25 mg** (twenty five milligrams) or **hydrochlorothiazide 25 to 50 mg** (twenty five to fifty milligrams) daily, cut **hypercalciuria** (excess urine calcium) by enhancing proximal and distal tubular calcium reabsorption. Pair the prescription with salt restriction and normal dietary calcium, because low calcium diets raise oxalate absorption. Watch potassium, glucose, and uric acid on follow up.
